title: The integral compactly supported direct image on localizing categories
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Use $\mathcal O_E$ as a condensed ring pulled back from the point, the unbounded derived category of module objects, and $\Dbc$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; $\Loc(\Dbc)$ is its localizing closure in that unbounded category, with ordinary small coproducts as in [sk-def-localizing-closure].

For a separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ and a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$, with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper, set $Rf_!^c=Rp_*D(j_!)$, the composite of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Then it restricts to an exact functor
$$Rf_!^c:\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E))$$
preserving small direct sums and carrying $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. These restrictions are canonically isomorphic for different compactifications, with identity and cocycle comparison maps. Writing $Rf_!$ for any chosen compactification, they have natural composition isomorphisms $Rg_!Rf_!\simeq R(gf)_!$ for composable separated finite-type $f,g$. For every cartesian square with $v:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'=X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ and $u:X'\to X$, the base-change map $v^*Rf_!\to Rf'_!u^*$ is an isomorphism on $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$. The composition and base-change isomorphisms are compatible with the compactification comparisons and restrict to $\Dbc$.

proof.text: First identify the coefficient categories, without changing the coefficient sheaf. A standing scheme is qcqs: finite type over a field includes quasi-compactness, and a separated diagonal is a closed immersion and hence quasi-compact. Apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ on each scheme that occurs. It gives $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and $\Loc(\Dctf)=\Loc(\Dbc)$ as full subcategories of the same ordinary unbounded module-object derived category. Thus the admissible-coefficient localizing theorems can be applied integrally. In particular, no ordinary coproduct is replaced by a completed coproduct.

source.place: First paragraph: the integral specialization and the equality $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$.

proof.text: Apply [det-cor-int-compactness-ii-extension-zero] to $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$. Its hypothesis is precisely the quasi-compact open immersion in the specified compactification. Its first clause says that extension by zero is exact and preserves all direct sums, its second that it preserves $\Dbc$, and its third that it maps the source localizing category into the target one. The derived notation $D(j_!)$ applies this exact functor termwise, so the same triangle and coproduct assertions hold for it.

source.place: Second paragraph, first bullet: extension by zero; only exactness, sums and the two preservation clauses are used.

proof.text: Apply [det-proper-image-localizing-proper] to $p:\overline X\to Y$ with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. Its final coefficient clause explicitly asserts that the required $\Dctf$ preservation and direct-sum preservation hold for this coefficient. Its conclusion therefore supplies an exact, sum-preserving restriction of $Rp_*$ to the localizing categories, and its asserted preservation of $\Dctf$ is preservation of $\Dbc$ under step 1. Both categories here use the same pulled-back integral ring as in step 2.

source.place: Second paragraph, second bullet: the integral proper-image preservation input, using its existing coefficient-specific localizing formulation.

proof.text:
The composite restriction is well-defined because the target localizing category of step 2 is the source localizing category of step 3. A distinguished triangle is sent to a distinguished triangle twice, with the composite shift comparison, so $Rp_*D(j_!)$ is exact. For a small family $(K_a)$, the canonical comparisons of steps 2 and 3 give
$$Rp_*j_!(\bigoplus_a K_a)\simeq Rp_*(\bigoplus_a j_!K_a)\simeq\bigoplus_a Rp_*j_!K_a.$$
If $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, then $j_!K\in\Dbc(\overline X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $Rp_*j_!K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. This also includes the empty coproduct and the zero complex.

source.place: Final paragraph, first sentence: form the composite and spell out its three properties.

proof.text: For compactifications $c_1,c_2$, apply [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ and use step 1 to read its domain as $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$. The hypothesis $Y$ qcqs was checked in step 1. The stated comparison $\phi_{c_2,c_1}$ is independent of the common dense refinement; its identity and cocycle equations are exactly the compatibility needed to identify all choices. Since both functors preserve $\Dbc$ by step 4, this same natural isomorphism restricts to $\Dbc$. This uses the existing comparison statement, rather than attributing comparison maps to the right-adjoint existence theorem.

source.place: Final paragraph: independence of compactification and the comparison isomorphisms.

proof.text:
For composition, first choose dense compactifications $f=pj$ and $g=qi$, with $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ open; step 5 will compare the resulting map with arbitrary chosen compactifications. The existence of dense choices follows from [sk-thm-nagata-compactification]. The scheme $\overline Y$ is standing and hence qcqs. Nagata [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] provides a dense compactification $\overline X\xrightarrow{j'}W\xrightarrow{r}\overline Y$ of the map $ip$. This map is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e); it is finite type because the quasi-compact open $i$ is finite type and $p$ is proper, hence finite type. The intermediate scheme $W$ is again standing, since its proper map to $\overline Y$ and the structure map of $\overline Y$ are separated of finite type, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Apply [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange] with $A=j_!K$. Step 2 and step 1 ensure $A\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\mathcal O_E))$, the precise hypothesis of its third clause. It gives the natural isomorphism
$$i_!Rp_*j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_*j'_!j_!K,$$
normalized by restriction to the identity of $Rp_*j_!K$ on $Y$. The same cited statement supplies $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$, so the normalization uses the actual pulled-back open.

source.place: The composition isomorphism: compactify the proper map followed by the open immersion and use the normalized interchange map.

proof.text: The formal composition identifications needed after step 6 have the following explicit sources. For opens $j,j'$, [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction] and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] give $j'_!j_!\dashv j^*j'^*$. The pullback composition comparison of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] identifies this right adjoint with $(j'j)^*$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to obtain the unique unit-compatible isomorphism $j'_!j_!\simeq(j'j)_!$; apply it termwise to get the derived identification. For proper maps $q,r$, use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to identify $Rq_*Rr_*\simeq R(qr)_*$. Its sheaf-module formulation applies to the present internal module objects via [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], which leaves underlying abelian sheaves and restrictions unchanged. Hence the sheaf direct image has exactly the target-ring action of the module-object direct image, and its K-injective total derived functor is the $Rp_*$ fixed in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. No assertion about deriving the underived composite $p_*j_!$ is used.

source.place: The composition isomorphism, final display; formal open and proper composition identities. Stacks Tag 0D6E (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), and Tag 0B65 for normalized adjoint uniqueness.

proof.text:
Apply $Rq_*$ to the isomorphism of step 6 and then the identifications of step 7:
$$Rg_!Rf_!K=Rq_*i_!Rp_*j_!K\simeq Rq_*Rr_*j'_!j_!K\simeq R(qr)_*(j'j)_!K.$$
The composite $j'j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion: after identifying both maps with inclusions of open subschemes, their composite is the inclusion of the same open $X$ in $W$, and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes it quasi-compact because $X$ is quasi-compact and $W$ is quasi-separated by step 1. The composite $qr$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a), and $(qr)(j'j)=gf$. Thus $(j'j,qr)$ is a compactification of $gf$. Postcompose with step 5 to reach the chosen compactification of $gf$. All maps in this display are natural in $K$.

Here is the refinement compatibility, including the normalization input. Write $e_h$ for the maps of [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement]; its clauses (1) and (3) give their identity normalization on the open and their transitivity. Common dense refinements needed below are supplied by [det-nagata-refinement-common-dense]; all bases are standing and hence qcqs. If only the auxiliary compactification $W$ of $ip$ is refined, its comparison before $Rq_*$ restricts to the identity on $Y$, since $e_h$ restricts to the identity on $\overline X$ and $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$. The two maps out of $i_!Rp_*j_!K$ therefore agree by [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](2), after the proper-composition identifications of step 7.

For a dense refinement $h:\overline X_1\to\overline X$ of the compactification of $f$, write $j_1:X\to\overline X_1$ and $p_1=ph$. Compactify $j'h:\overline X_1\to W$ densely as $\overline X_1\xrightarrow{a}V\xrightarrow{s}W$, using Nagata. Interchange clause (1), applied to the proper map $h$ and the open $j'$, gives $s^{-1}(\overline X)=\overline X_1$. Thus $s:V\to W$ is a refinement of the induced compactifications of $gf$, and $(a,rs)$ is a dense compactification of $ip_1$. The comparison $e_s$ for the open $X$ restricts over $\overline X$ to $e_h$: both maps $j_!K\to Rh_*j_{1!}K$ restrict to the identity on $X$, so refinement clause (1) identifies them. Consequently the two composition paths, before $Rq_*$, restrict on $Y$ to $Rp_*e_h$. Identify their source with $i_!R(ph)_*j_{1!}K$ by this isomorphism. Both paths now restrict to the identity, and interchange clause (2) for $ip_1$ equates them.

For a dense refinement $b:\overline Y_1\to\overline Y$ of the compactification of $g$, write $i_1:Y\to\overline Y_1$, so $bi_1=i$ and the new proper part is $qb$. Choose a dense compactification $(t,r_1)$ of $i_1p$. Then $(t,br_1)$ compactifies $ip$. Compare this compactification with $(j',r)$ through a common dense refinement. Before $Rq_*$, one path first uses $e_b$ on $Rp_*j_!K$ and then applies $Rb_*$ to interchange for $i_1p$; the other first uses interchange for $ip$ and then the comparison to $(t,br_1)$. Both restrict on $Y$ to the identity of $Rp_*j_!K$, by refinement clause (1). Interchange clause (2), applied to the compactification $(t,br_1)$ of $ip$, equates them. Transitivity of the refinement maps and the cocycle of [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] therefore give compatibility for any pair of dense choices. Finally define the composition maps for arbitrary compactifications by pre- and postcomposing with the comparisons of step 5; the cocycle equations make these maps commute with every further compactification comparison. Every functor in the composition display preserves $\Dbc$ by steps 2–4, so the same maps restrict there.

source.place: The composition isomorphism, final display, and Canonicity: use the open normalization and the comparison cocycle.

proof.text:
For a cartesian square in the statement, $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ is admissible and $Y'$ is standing, hence qcqs. Apply [det-sf-comp-composition-base-change] to the specified compactification of $f$ and its pullback. Its clauses (1) and (2) supply precisely
$$v^*Rp_*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*v'^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*j'_!u^*,$$
as functors on $\Loc(\Dctf)$, which is $\Loc(\Dbc)$ by step 1. Clause (3) makes this map compatible with comparisons to the chosen compactification of $f'$, giving the claimed base-change map independently of choices. Finally [sk-lem-int-tensor] asserts that $u^*,v^*$ preserve $\Dbc$, while step 4 gives the same assertion for the compact-support functors. Thus the very same isomorphism restricts to $\Dbc$. The base change is for the module-object pulled-back integral coefficient system throughout.

statement_correction.old_statement:
For a separated morphism of finite type $f:X\to Y$ with compactification
$f=p\circ j$ ($j$ an open immersion, $p$ proper), put
$Rf_!=Rp_*\circ j_!:\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))\to\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E))$.
Then $Rf_!$ is a well-defined exact functor preserving direct sums, it maps
$\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, and up to canonical
isomorphism it is independent of the compactification, compatible with
composition and with base change.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q11-fba58588a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 9 steps and every one of the 26 cited node statements, plus the main-20261015 blueprint construction text and proof, the unit and chapter records, and the duplicate candidates. The statement correction holds. My own check of the counterexample: for R the product of F_p over N and m a non-principal ultrafilter point, Spec F_p -> Spec R is proper, but i_*O_E is not constructible, because constructible subsets of Spec R are clopen and {m} is not open. Restoring the standing setting sk-def-sfb-dc-setting matches the sibling nodes sk-prop-sf-existence and det-sf-comp-coherence-single, keeps every conclusion, and touches no target. The 'quasi-compact open' condition is automatic in that setting. Coefficients are module objects over the pulled-back O_E in the ordinary unbounded D(Mod) with ordinary coproducts, not the derived-complete Rlim category of def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, so same_as=[] is right. The base-change map v^*Rf_! -> Rf'_!u^* is beta of det-sf-comp-composition-base-change(2). Step checks: S1 ctf-equals-bc(2), qcqs holds. S2 extension-by-zero clauses 1-3, on-route. S3 the O_E clause of det-proper-image-localizing-proper asserts its own hypotheses. S4 elementary. S5 cocycle hypotheses hold. S6 Nagata (Lean-closed) plus interchange (1)-(3) with A=j_!K. S7 open composition via the adjunction, the pullback-composition comparison and conjugate uniqueness, and proper composition via the ringed-topoi lemma and the internal-module equivalence. S8 checked qrj'j=gf; each refinement case (W, f, g) reduces to interchange (2) or refinement (1)/(3) uniqueness. S9 Y' qcqs, clauses 1-3, and Dbc restriction via sk-lem-int-tensor. Small cases checked: identities, pure open or pure proper f, empty scheme, zero complex, empty coproduct, v=id. No cycle, proof_deps equals the union of uses, no SGA, three kinds of Mathlib search recorded. No new nodes. One optional simplification: steps 1-4 re-derive the existing det-sf-comp-coherence-single instead of citing it, which is correct but not required.
